images.title: Plum cake on the plate
images.purpose: Set up the question 5/8 − 3/8: a cake cut into 8 equal slices with 5 slices on the plate, ready for the student to take away 3 slices and simplify.
images.composition: One round cake on a plain plate on the left with plenty of space, and a short column of text lines on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one flat round cake seen from above, on a plain round plate, cut by 4 straight lines through the centre into exactly 8 equal slices. 5 neighbouring slices are filled teal #0072B2; the other 3 slice places are empty outlines in grey #6B7280. A small reddish purple #CC79A7 bracket marks one teal slice. Right: a column of 5 short text lines with wide spacing. No slice is shown being eaten. Exactly 1 cake, 8 equal slices, 5 teal, 3 empty.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any result of the subtraction shown in numbers, or slices of unequal size
images.takeaway: Count slices of the same unit, then simplify.
images.description: A cake cut into 8 equal slices with 5 teal slices on the plate; the question asks for 5/8 − 3/8 in lowest terms, with no answer shown.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one slice, name its unit, and say how many slices stay after 3 are eaten.

image_decisions.why: Seeing equal slices of one cake sets up the take away without giving the answer; one clean picture carries it.
